sections.heading: Persistent Account Storage
paragraphs: Per the file, the set of accts represent the current computed (per the file) state of all the txs that have been processed by a node. Per the file, each node needs to maintain this entire set. Per the file, each block that is (per the file) proposed by the network (per the file) represents a change to (per the file) this set, and since (per the file) each block is a (per the file) potential rollback point, the (per the file) changes need to be reversible.

Per the file, persistent storage like NVMEs (per the file) are 20 to 40 (per the file) times cheaper than DDR. Per the file, the problem with persistent (per the file) storage is that write (per the file) and read performance is (per the file) much slower than DDR. Per the file, care has to be taken in how (per the file) data is read or written to. Per the file, both reads and writes may be split between multiple (per the file) storage drives and accessed in parallel.

Per the file, this design proposes a data structure that lets for concurrent reads and (per the file) concurrent writes of storage. Per the file, writes are optimized by (per the file) using an AppendVec data structure, which lets a single writer to (per the file) append while allowing access (per the file) to many concurrent readers. Per the file, the accts index maintains a pointer (per the file) to a spot where the acct was appended to every (per the file) fork, thus removing the (per the file) need for explicit checkpointing of state. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: AppendVec
paragraphs: Per the file, appendVec is a data structure that lets for random reads concurrent (per the file) with a single append-only writer. Per the file, growing or resizing the (per the file) capacity of the AppendVec calls for exclusive access. Per the file, this is implemented with (per the file) an atomic offset, which (per the file) is updated at the (per the file) end of a completed append. Per the file, the underlying memory for (per the file) an AppendVec is a memory-mapped file. Per the file, memory-mapped files allow (per the file) for fast random access and (per the file) paging is handled by the OS. sections.heading: Account Index
paragraphs: Per the file, the acct index is meant to support a single (per the file) index for all the currently forked Accounts. Per the file, the index is a map of acct Pubkeys to a map (per the file) of Forks and the (per the file) location of the Account (per the file) data in an AppendVec. Per the file, to get the version of an acct for a specific Fork: The read is satisfied (per the file) by pointing to a (per the file) memory-mapped location in the (per the file) AppendVecId at the stored offset. Per the file, a reference may be returned without a copy. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Root Forks
paragraphs: Per the file, tower BFT eventually selects a fork (per the file) as a root fork (per the file) and the fork is squashed. Per the file, a squashed/root fork cannot (per the file) be rolled back. Per the file, when a fork is squashed, all accts in its parents not (per the file) already present in the (per the file) fork are pulled up (per the file) into the fork by updating the indexes. Per the file, accounts with zero balance (per the file) in the squashed fork (per the file) are removed from fork (per the file) by updating the indexes.

Per the file, an acct may be _garbage-collected_ when squashing (per the file) makes it unreachable. Per the file, three possible options exist: (per the file) Maintain a HashSet of root forks. Per the file, one is expected to (per the file) be created every second. Per the file, the entire tree may be garbage-collected later. Per the file, alternatively, if every fork (per the file) keeps a reference count of accts, garbage collection could occur (per the file) any time an index location is updated.

Per the file, remove any pruned forks from the index. Per the file, any remaining forks lower (per the file) in number than the root are may be considered root. Per the file, scan the index, migrate (per the file) any old roots into the new one. Per the file, any remaining forks lower (per the file) than the new root may be deleted later. sections.heading: Garbage collection
paragraphs: Per the file, as accts get updated, they move (per the file) to the end of the AppendVec. Per the file, once capacity has run (per the file) out, a new AppendVec may be created and updates may be stored there. Per the file, eventually references to an (per the file) older AppendVec will disappear because all the accts have been updated, and the old AppendVec may be deleted. Per the file, to speed up this (per the file) process, it's possible to (per the file) move Accounts that have not (per the file) been recently updated to the (per the file) front of a new AppendVec.

Per the file, this form of garbage collection may be done without requiring (per the file) exclusive locks to any (per the file) of the data structures (per the file) except for the index update. Per the file, the initial implementation for (per the file) garbage collection is that once all the accts in an AppendVec become (per the file) stale versions, it gets reused. Per the file, the accts are not updated or (per the file) moved around once appended.

sections.heading: Index Recovery
paragraphs: Per the file, each bank thread has (per the file) exclusive access to the accts during append, since the accts locks cannot be released (per the file) until the data is committed. Per the file, but there is no (per the file) explicit order of writes (per the file) between the separate AppendVec files. Per the file, to create an ordering, (per the file) the index maintains an (per the file) atomic write version counter. Per the file, each append to the (per the file) AppendVec records the index (per the file) write version number for (per the file) that append in the (per the file) entry for the Account in the AppendVec.

Per the file, to recover the index, (per the file) all the AppendVec files may be read in any (per the file) order, and the latest (per the file) write version for every fork ought to be stored in the index. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Snapshots
paragraphs: Per the file, to snapshot, the underlying (per the file) memory-mapped files in the (per the file) AppendVec need to be flushed to disk. Per the file, the index may be written out to disk as well. Those statements are the file’s claims, not a Sol.College measurement of a live cluster.

sections.heading: Performance
paragraphs: Per the file, append-only writes are fast. Per the file, sSDs and NVMEs, and also all the OS level (per the file) kernel data structures, allow (per the file) for appends to run (per the file) as fast as PCI (per the file) or NVMe bandwidth will (per the file) allow \(2,700 MB/s\). Per the file, each replay and banking (per the file) thread writes concurrently to its own AppendVec. Per the file, each AppendVec could potentially (per the file) be hosted on a separate NVMe.

Per the file, each replay and banking (per the file) thread has concurrent read (per the file) access to all the (per the file) AppendVecs without blocking writes. Per the file, index calls for an exclusive write lock for writes. Per the file, single-thread performance for HashMap (per the file) updates is on the order (per the file) of 10m per second. Per the file, banking and Replay stages (per the file) should use 32 threads per NVMe. Per the file, nVMes have optimal performance (per the file) with 32 concurrent readers or writers.
